From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Tom Baker <t.baker@payyard.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-09T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG & gating for procurement — technical artifacts

Adding technical detail and attachments. Marissa — attaching the KMS architecture diagram and a short SOC 2 evidence summary that maps our control responses to artifacts. Notes inline in the spreadsheet (tab: evidence_map).

Highlights:
- Keys: customer data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; each tenant uses a unique CMK in our KMS (managed by customer or Redwood depending on plan). Rotation: 90-day automatic rotation for ephemeral keys; CMKs rotated per AR (annual) — see kms-arch-diagram.png.
- Access: strict least-privilege IAM roles for runtime and admin — we include a sample policy and recent audit log extract.
- Retention: default logs keep 90 days; application data retention depends on customer config, default 365 days.

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf, kms-arch-diagram.png

If Payyard needs raw audit logs for an early review, we can provide an export under NDA — confirm required window.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf]
[attachment: kms-arch-diagram.png]

Marissa — thanks for the updates and the diagram. A couple quick clarifications before procurement starts formal review:
1) We need one artifact showing KMS ownership for our account (is customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private customers?).
2) Can you provide the last 30 days of audit log hashes or a recent export sample (redacted) so we can validate integrity claims?
3) Retention: procurement wants a concise statement we can insert into the SOW about default retention and options to change it.

If you can get items 1 and 3 by EOD 6/15 that will keep us on the June 19 gate; item 2 can follow under NDA.

— Payyard Sec Team
security@payyard.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Date: 2026-06-15T10:30:00-07:00

Marissa — drafting a short addendum that states: "Default retention is 365 days for application data and 90 days for platform logs; Customer may request extensions or shorter windows via the Console or SOW. KMS: customer-managed keys available on Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers may opt into managed CMK with bring-your-own-key for an additional ops agreement."

I’ll drop the exact snippet into the shared drive; if Payyard wants stronger contractual guarantees (specific retention windows in SOW) we should be ready to push for a 12-month committed retention with amendment.

— Jonas
